1.
Heard Ms. Smriti, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Jayant Singh Tomar, learned A.G.A.-I for the State and perused the record.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
437 of 2022, under Section 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, registered at Police Station Maurawan, District Unnao.

The applicant took her to some place, he took a room and committed the misdeed against her.
He dropped her back to Hilaula after two days.
5. The medico legal examination report of the victim reveals no mark of injury or sign of use of force.
6. In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she stated that the applicant committed the misdeed against her in a room in Anand Vihar, Delhi.
7. In the affidavit filed in support of the bail application, it has been stated that the applicant is innocent, he has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has no criminal history.

8. The State has filed a counter affidavit annexing therewith copies of material collected during investigation and a copy of the charge-sheet dated 16.06.2024.
9.
A Supplementary affidavit has been filed on behalf of the applicant annexing therewith copies of statements of the informant, the victim and the victim's mother recorded by the trial court.

The informant and his wife have supported the prosecution case and the victim has also supported the prosecution case but the victim as well as her mother both have not supported the same during their cross-examination.
During the cross-examination, the victim has stated that at the time of the incident she was aged 19 years.

10. The learned A.G.A-I has vehemently opposed the bail application and he has submitted that the victim has fully supported the prosecution case in her statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C as well as during her examination-in-chief.
It appears that the accused persons has threatened or given allurement to the victim due to which she has resiled from her earlier statements during her cross-examination.

11. When we examine the facts and circumstances of the case as appear from the entire material available on record, it appears that the F.I.R was lodged on 05.09.2022 wherein the informant stated that the applicant had enticed away his daughter at about 04:00 PM on 27.08.2024.

In the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C, she has stated that the applicant had taken her away to some place, which she did not disclose, took a room committed the misdeed against her and dropped her back to Hilaula merely after two days thereafter, whereas the F.I.R has been lodged nine days after the incident; the allegations levelled by the informant and the victim are not supported by the findings of the medico legal examination report; that the applicant is a young man having no criminal history and he is languishing in jail since 10.09.2022 and the statements of all the witnesses of fact have already been examined and in case of his release the applicant will not be in a position to influence the witnesses, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for enlargement of the applicant on bail.
12. Accordingly, this bail application stands allowed.

13. Let the applicant- Deep Chandra be released on bail in the aforementioned case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Magistrate/Court Deep Chandra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

15. The trial court shall pass appropriate orders in this regard and the State authorities shall ensure necessary action for recovering the public money paid to the vicitm for the reason that she was a victim of the alleged offence, which allegation she has herself withdrawn.
